raw_response.rationale: Full text (17 PDF pages) is accessible and reports inferential Tobit regressions (Table 4, p. 994; Table 5, p. 997; N = 160 households across 16 rural water systems in Achefer, Ethiopia). However, the study fails Criterion 4 (and narrow Criterion 2) for SWiM synthesis: the sole dependent variables in the econometric models are households' voluntary cash contributions (CASHCONT, in ETB) and voluntary labour contributions (LABORCONT, in days) over the preceding 3 months toward system protection and maintenance (described by the authors as willingness-to-pay cash and willingness-to-contribute labour). No household or community water supply service access outcome (such as connection, coverage, functionality/reliability, continuity, quantity, water quality, or affordability/exclusion) is analysed as a dependent variable (subjective water satisfaction WASATS and perceived source safety PSOWS enter only as explanatory covariates predicting O&M contributions and are statistically insignificant). Moreover, the main significant predictors (self-rated degree of participation during NGO project design/implementation, health-promoter advocacy, household income, and trust in WUCs) are participatory project-delivery, attitudinal, and socioeconomic factors rather than a rule-type legal/administrative/tariff/tenure exposure tested on service access.
